---
title: Call an agent
description: agent.invoke runs an agent from your own code, with no chat on the page; useWebAgent adds live status in a component.
sidebar:
  label: 9. Call an agent
---

An agent has the same verb as a tool: **`invoke`**. Give it a sentence, and it decides which tools to call: the model
asks for a tool, the tool runs on the page under the cursor, the result goes back, until the model answers. It is the
chat's loop without the chat, for a button that does a whole task ("Track my last order"), a command palette, or an
onboarding step.

## A complete example

One task, "Track my last order", run two ways. Pick the tab that fits where the call is made:

import { shopper } from "@/agents";

Both need the `/api/chat` route from [Add the chat](/build/add-the-chat), but not the widget: by default an agent runs
on the same shared adapter, which talks to that route. Both run in the browser, on a page inside your provider, so
the agent sees the page's tools.

## What `useWebAgent` gives you

`useWebAgent(agent, { adapter? })` returns:

| | |
|---|---|
| `invoke(text)` | Start a run. A second call stops the first. It never rejects: it resolves `undefined` when the run was stopped or failed, so `onClick={() => agent.invoke("…")}` needs no `catch`. |
| `status` | `idle`, `running`, `waiting` (a tool is parked on the page until the person clicks), or `error`. |
| `steps` | The tool calls of the current or last run, live, each with its `tool`, `input` and `state`. A sub-agent's calls are included, with `agent` set. |
| `text` | The agent's answer so far, streamed. |
| `error` | Why the last run failed, with a `code`. Cleared by the next `invoke`. |
| `stop()` | Cancel the run in flight. |

Each `invoke` is a fresh conversation: the agent remembers nothing from the last one.

## What `agent.invoke` gives you

`agent.invoke(text, { adapter?, signal?, onStep? })` is the same run with no component around it. It resolves to `{ text, steps, messages }`: the answer, every tool call it made, and the whole conversation. Unlike the
hook, it **rejects**: with the adapter's message and `code` when the run fails, with an `AbortError` when its `signal`
aborts, for an empty message, and on the server. `invoke` runs in the browser, because the agent's tools are the
page's; on the server, register the agent with `createChatHandler({ agents })` instead.

The agent file stays plain data that a server can import: `invoke` loads the browser loop on its first call.

## Another model for one call

Both take an `adapter`. Pass [`createLocalAdapter()`](/more/on-device-agent) to run the same agent on a model in the
browser, with no server and no key, or a `createCloudAdapter({ … })` of your own. Create an adapter once, at module
scope, not on every render.

## Try it

Render `<TrackLastOrder />` inside your provider, start the app with the key in `.env.local`, and click **Track my last
order**. The button reads "Working…", the list fills with `delegate_to_orders`, then the helper's `go_to`,
`list_orders` and `track_order`, the cursor moves to `/orders`, and the answer appears below. Keep a link to `/orders`
in your layout: `go_to` clicks it, so your router navigates without reloading the page (a reload would end the run).

## Options you'll use most

| Option | Where | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| `adapter` | both | What runs the model. Default: one shared cloud adapter that talks to `/api/chat`. |
| `signal` | `agent.invoke` | Stop the run: the model, the tool in flight, any sub-agent. |
| `onStep(step)` | `agent.invoke` | Called when a tool call starts, parks on the person's confirmation, or ends. |

Reference: [`useWebAgent`](/reference/chat/use-web-agent) and [`defineWebAgent`](/reference/chat/define-web-agent)
(the agent's `invoke`).
